pattern: 〜ちゃいけない / 〜じゃいけない
meaning: Casual 'you mustn't': the spoken short form of 〜てはいけない. 〜ては becomes 〜ちゃ, and 〜では becomes 〜じゃ.

examples.ja: ここで{写真|しゃしん}を{撮|と}っ[[ちゃいけない]]よ。
examples.en: You can't take photos here.

examples.ja: {授業中|じゅぎょうちゅう}に{寝|ね}[[ちゃいけない]]よ。
examples.en: You mustn't sleep in class.

examples.ja: この{川|かわ}で{泳|およ}い[[じゃいけない]]よ。
examples.en: You can't swim in this river.

examples.ja: {子供|こども}はお{酒|さけ}を{飲|の}ん[[じゃいけない]]。
examples.en: Children mustn't drink alcohol.

questions.ja: テストの{時|とき}、ノートを[[{見|み}ちゃいけない]]よ。
questions.en: You mustn't look at your notes during the test.
questions.explain: 見る is an ichidan verb: 見て becomes 見ちゃ.

questions.ja: {道|みち}で[[{遊|あそ}んじゃいけない]]よ。
questions.en: You mustn't play in the street.
questions.explain: 遊ぶ becomes 遊んで, and a て-form ending in で turns into じゃ.

pattern: Noun / な-adj + だ / です
meaning: The copula 'is / am / are' after a noun or な-adjective. です is polite; だ is the plain form for friends and for writing.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}は{学生|がくせい}[[です]]。
examples.en: I'm a student.

examples.ja: あの{人|ひと}は{木村|きむら}さんのお{兄|にい}さん[[だ]]よ。
examples.en: That's Kimura's older brother.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}は{休|やす}み[[です]]か。
examples.en: Is tomorrow a day off?

examples.ja: それは{私|わたし}の{傘|かさ}[[だ]]よ。
examples.en: That's my umbrella.

questions.ja: この{本|ほん}はとても{面白|おもしろ}い[[です]]。
questions.en: This book is very interesting.
questions.explain: い-adjectives take です to be polite, never だ; the past would be 面白かったです.

questions.ja: この{部屋|へや}はいつも{静|しず}か[[だ]]ね。
questions.en: This room is always quiet, isn't it?
questions.explain: In casual speech a な-adjective ends the sentence with だ; な only goes before a noun.

meaning: 'Only, just': limits things to what comes before it and nothing more.

examples.ja: {朝|あさ}はコーヒー[[だけ]]{飲|の}みます。
examples.en: In the morning I only drink coffee.

examples.ja: {日本語|にほんご}は{少|すこ}し[[だけ]]{分|わ}かります。
examples.en: I understand just a little Japanese.

examples.ja: この{店|みせ}は{日曜日|にちようび}[[だけ]]{休|やす}みです。
examples.en: This shop is closed only on Sundays.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}のパーティーには{一人|ひとり}[[だけ]]{来|き}ました。
examples.en: Only one person came to yesterday's party.

questions.ja: {財布|さいふ}に{千円|せんえん}[[だけ]]あります。
questions.en: I only have 1,000 yen in my wallet.
questions.explain: だけ goes with an affirmative verb; しか would need ありません.

questions.ja: すみません、{見|み}ている[[だけ]]です。
questions.en: Sorry, I'm just looking.
questions.explain: Verb + だけです means 'I'm only doing this'.

meaning: Plain form of でしょう: 'probably', or 'right?' when you expect the listener to agree. Used in casual speech and in writing.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}は{雨|あめ}[[だろう]]。
examples.en: It'll probably rain tomorrow.

examples.ja: {木村|きむら}さんはもう{家|いえ}に{帰|かえ}った[[だろう]]。
examples.en: Kimura has probably gone home by now.

examples.ja: あの{店|みせ}は{高|たか}い[[だろう]]。
examples.en: That shop is probably expensive.

examples.ja: {一緒|いっしょ}に{行|い}く[[だろう]]？
examples.en: You're coming with us, right?

questions.ja: {明日|あした}はたぶん{晴|は}れ[[だろう]]。
questions.en: It'll probably be sunny tomorrow.
questions.explain: だろう attaches straight to a noun, with no だ or な, and is never followed by です.

questions.ja: {木村|きむら}さんはもう{駅|えき}に{着|つ}い[[ただろう]]。
questions.en: Kimura has probably reached the station by now.
questions.explain: Put だろう after the plain past form: 着いた + だろう.

meaning: Marks where an action takes place, or the tool, language or transport used to do it.

examples.ja: {図書館|としょかん}[[で]]{本|ほん}を{読|よ}みます。
examples.en: I read books at the library.

examples.ja: {毎朝|まいあさ}バス[[で]]{会社|かいしゃ}へ{行|い}きます。
examples.en: I go to work by bus every morning.

examples.ja: {日本語|にほんご}[[で]]{手紙|てがみ}を{書|か}きました。
examples.en: I wrote a letter in Japanese.

examples.ja: {箸|はし}[[で]]ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べます。
examples.en: I eat rice with chopsticks.

questions.ja: {食堂|しょくどう}[[で]]{昼|ひる}ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べました。
questions.en: I had lunch in the cafeteria.
questions.explain: The place where an action happens takes で.

questions.ja: {日本語|にほんご}[[で]]{話|はな}してください。
questions.en: Please speak in Japanese.
questions.explain: The language you speak in takes で.

meaning: 'But' or 'however' at the start of a sentence, setting it against the one before. Common in conversation.

examples.ja: {日本語|にほんご}は{難|むずか}しいです。[[でも]]、{面白|おもしろ}いです。
examples.en: Japanese is hard. But it's interesting.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}は{雨|あめ}でした。[[でも]]、{公園|こうえん}へ{行|い}きました。
examples.en: It rained yesterday. But I went to the park anyway.

examples.ja: この{店|みせ}は{安|やす}いです。[[でも]]、あまりおいしくないです。
examples.en: This place is cheap. But the food isn't very good.

examples.ja: {行|い}きたいです。[[でも]]、{時間|じかん}がありません。
examples.en: I want to go. But I don't have time.

questions.ja: この{靴|くつ}はとても{高|たか}いです。[[でも]]、{買|か}いました。
questions.en: These shoes are very expensive. But I bought them.
questions.explain: でも can open a sentence; から, ので and のに must attach to the end of a clause.

questions.ja: {兄|あに}は{背|せ}が{高|たか}いです。[[でも]]、{弟|おとうと}は{低|ひく}いです。
questions.en: My older brother is tall. But my younger brother is short.
questions.explain: Only でも can start a new sentence to show contrast.

meaning: 'Probably' when making a polite guess; with a rising tone, 'right?' to check that the listener agrees.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}は{晴|は}れる[[でしょう]]。
examples.en: It will probably be sunny tomorrow.

examples.ja: {木村|きむら}さんは{来|こ}ない[[でしょう]]。
examples.en: Kimura probably won't come.

examples.ja: あのレストランは{高|たか}い[[でしょう]]ね。
examples.en: That restaurant must be expensive.

examples.ja: この{本|ほん}、{面白|おもしろ}かった[[でしょう]]？
examples.en: This book was good, wasn't it?

questions.ja: {今晩|こんばん}は{雪|ゆき}が{降|ふ}る[[でしょう]]。
questions.en: It will probably snow tonight.
questions.explain: でしょう follows the plain form directly; ましょう means 'let's' and goes on a verb stem.

questions.ja: あの{人|ひと}はたぶん{学生|がくせい}[[でしょう]]。
questions.en: That person is probably a student.
questions.explain: でしょう attaches straight to a noun, with no だ or な.

meaning: 'What kind of…?': asks what something or someone is like. It always comes directly before a noun.

examples.ja: [[どんな]]{音楽|おんがく}が{好|す}きですか。
examples.en: What kind of music do you like?

examples.ja: {新|あたら}しいアパートは[[どんな]]{所|ところ}ですか。
examples.en: What's your new apartment like?

examples.ja: [[どんな]]スポーツをしますか。
examples.en: What sports do you play?

examples.ja: あなたの{町|まち}は[[どんな]]{町|まち}ですか。
examples.en: What's your town like?

questions.ja: [[どんな]]{食|た}べ{物|もの}が{好|す}きですか。
questions.en: What kind of food do you like?
questions.explain: どんな comes right before a noun to ask 'what kind of'.

questions.ja: {木村|きむら}さんのお{姉|ねえ}さんは[[どんな]]{人|ひと}ですか。
questions.en: What is Kimura's older sister like?
questions.explain: To ask what a person is like, use どんな + 人.

meaning: 'Why?': asks for a reason. The reply usually ends in 〜から or 〜からです.

examples.ja: [[どうして]]{昨日|きのう}{学校|がっこう}を{休|やす}んだんですか。
examples.en: Why were you off school yesterday?

examples.ja: [[どうして]]{日本語|にほんご}を{勉強|べんきょう}しているんですか。
examples.en: Why are you studying Japanese?

examples.ja: [[どうして]]{何|なに}も{食|た}べないんですか。
examples.en: Why aren't you eating anything?

examples.ja: 「[[どうして]]{傘|かさ}を{持|も}っているんですか。」「{午後|ごご}、{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}るからです。」
examples.en: "Why have you got an umbrella?" "Because it's going to rain this afternoon."

questions.ja: 「[[どうして]]{窓|まど}を{開|あ}けたんですか。」「{暑|あつ}かったからです。」
questions.en: "Why did you open the window?" "Because it was hot."
questions.explain: The reply gives a reason (〜からです), so the question asks 'why'.

questions.ja: 「[[どうして]]{何|なに}も{言|い}わなかったんですか。」「よく{分|わ}からなかったからです。」
questions.en: "Why didn't you say anything?" "Because I didn't really understand."
questions.explain: The reply gives a reason, so the question needs どうして.

meaning: 'How?', 'by what means?': asks about the method or route for doing something.

examples.ja: {駅|えき}まで[[どうやって]]{行|い}きますか。
examples.en: How do I get to the station?

examples.ja: この{漢字|かんじ}は[[どうやって]]{読|よ}みますか。
examples.en: How do you read this kanji?

examples.ja: [[どうやって]]{日本語|にほんご}を{勉強|べんきょう}しましたか。
examples.en: How did you study Japanese?

examples.ja: このカメラは[[どうやって]]{使|つか}うんですか。
examples.en: How do you use this camera?

questions.ja: 「{会社|かいしゃ}まで[[どうやって]]{来|き}ますか。」「{自転車|じてんしゃ}で{来|き}ます。」
questions.en: "How do you get to work?" "I come by bike."
questions.explain: The reply gives a means (自転車で), so the question asks 'how'.

questions.ja: この{料理|りょうり}は[[どうやって]]{作|つく}りますか。
questions.en: How do you make this dish?
questions.explain: どうやって asks the method and goes before a verb; どんな needs a noun after it.

meaning: Marks the subject, especially new information or the answer to 'who?' or 'what?'. Also marks the object of words like 好き, 上手 and 分かる.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}は{猫|ねこ}[[が]]{好|す}きです。
examples.en: I like cats.

examples.ja: あ、{雨|あめ}[[が]]{降|ふ}っていますね。
examples.en: Oh, it's raining.

examples.ja: マリアさんは{英語|えいご}[[が]]{分|わ}かります。
examples.en: Maria understands English.

examples.ja: 「{誰|だれ}が{作|つく}りましたか。」「{母|はは}[[が]]{作|つく}りました。」
examples.en: "Who made it?" "My mother made it."

questions.ja: {誰|だれ}[[が]]この{手紙|てがみ}を{書|か}きましたか。
questions.en: Who wrote this letter?
questions.explain: Question words like 誰 take が as the subject, never は.

questions.ja: {木村|きむら}さんはテニス[[が]]{上手|じょうず}です。
questions.en: Kimura is good at tennis.
questions.explain: 上手 marks the skill with が.

meaning: 'There is' or 'I have' for things and events. People and animals take います instead.

examples.ja: {机|つくえ}の{上|うえ}に{本|ほん}が[[あります]]。
examples.en: There's a book on the desk.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}、テストが[[あります]]。
examples.en: I have a test tomorrow.

examples.ja: この{近|ちか}くに{銀行|ぎんこう}が[[あります]]か。
examples.en: Is there a bank near here?

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}は{時間|じかん}が[[ありません]]。
examples.en: I don't have time today.

questions.ja: {部屋|へや}にテレビが[[あります]]。
questions.en: There's a TV in the room.
questions.explain: A TV is a thing, so it takes あります.

questions.ja: {財布|さいふ}にお{金|かね}が[[ありません]]。
questions.en: There's no money in my wallet.
questions.explain: Money is a thing; the negative of あります is ありません.

meaning: 'I want (something)': for objects you'd like to have. ほしい conjugates like an い-adjective; for actions use 〜たい.

examples.ja: {新|あたら}しいパソコンが[[ほしい]]です。
examples.en: I want a new computer.

examples.ja: {誕生日|たんじょうび}に{何|なに}が[[ほしい]]ですか。
examples.en: What do you want for your birthday?

examples.ja: {前|まえ}は{大|おお}きい{車|くるま}が[[ほしかった]]です。
examples.en: I used to want a big car.

examples.ja: {今|いま}は{何|なに}も[[ほしくない]]です。
examples.en: I don't want anything right now.

questions.ja: {子供|こども}の{時|とき}、{自転車|じてんしゃ}が[[ほしかったです]]。
questions.en: When I was a child, I wanted a bike.
questions.explain: ほしい is an い-adjective, so its past is ほしかったです.

questions.ja: もっと{広|ひろ}い{部屋|へや}が[[ほしいです]]。
questions.en: I want a bigger room.
questions.explain: For things you want, use ほしい; たい attaches to verbs.

meaning: 'There is' or 'I have' for people and animals. Things take あります.

examples.ja: {公園|こうえん}に{子供|こども}が[[います]]。
examples.en: There are children in the park.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}は{兄|あに}が{二人|ふたり}[[います]]。
examples.en: I have two older brothers.

examples.ja: {木|き}の{上|うえ}に{鳥|とり}が[[います]]。
examples.en: There's a bird up in the tree.

examples.ja: {教室|きょうしつ}に{先生|せんせい}が[[いません]]。
examples.en: The teacher isn't in the classroom.

questions.ja: {庭|にわ}に{猫|ねこ}が[[います]]。
questions.en: There's a cat in the garden.
questions.explain: A cat is alive, so it takes います.

questions.ja: {日曜日|にちようび}は{会社|かいしゃ}に{誰|だれ}も[[いません]]。
questions.en: There's nobody at the office on Sundays.
questions.explain: 誰も needs a negative, and people take いる: いません.

pattern: 〜たほうがいい / 〜ないほうがいい
meaning: 'You'd better' or 'it's best to': gives advice. Use the past form (〜た) to advise doing something and 〜ない to advise against it.

examples.ja: {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}っていますから、タクシーで{行|い}った[[ほうがいい]]ですよ。
examples.en: It's raining, so you'd better take a taxi.

examples.ja: {夜|よる}はあまり{食|た}べない[[ほうがいい]]です。
examples.en: It's better not to eat much at night.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}は{寒|さむ}いですから、コートを{着|き}た[[ほうがいい]]ですよ。
examples.en: It's cold today, so you'd better wear a coat.

examples.ja: {疲|つか}れている{時|とき}は、{早|はや}く{寝|ね}た[[ほうがいい]]です。
examples.en: When you're tired, it's best to go to bed early.

questions.ja: {風邪|かぜ}ですか。{薬|くすり}を[[{飲|の}んだ]]ほうがいいですよ。
questions.en: Have you got a cold? You'd better take some medicine.
questions.explain: To advise doing something, use the past た-form + ほうがいい.

questions.ja: {危|あぶ}ないですから、この{川|かわ}で[[{泳|およ}がない]]ほうがいいです。
questions.en: It's dangerous, so you'd better not swim in this river.
questions.explain: To advise against something, use the ない-form: 泳ぐ becomes 泳がない.

pattern: 〜い / 〜くない / 〜かった / 〜くなかった
meaning: Adjectives ending in い change that ending for negative and past: 高い, 高くない, 高かった, 高くなかった. いい works from よい: よくない, よかった.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}はとても[[{暑|あつ}い]]です。
examples.en: It's very hot today.

examples.ja: この{部屋|へや}はあまり[[{広|ひろ}くない]]です。
examples.en: This room isn't very big.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}のテストは[[{難|むずか}しかった]]です。
examples.en: Yesterday's test was difficult.

examples.ja: {旅行|りょこう}はとても[[よかった]]です。
examples.en: The trip was really good.

questions.ja: {昨日|きのう}はとても[[{寒|さむ}かったです]]。
questions.en: It was very cold yesterday.
questions.explain: The past of 寒い is 寒かった; い-adjectives never take でした.

questions.ja: この{映画|えいが}はあまり[[よくなかったです]]。
questions.en: This film wasn't very good.
wrong: いいじゃなかったです
questions.explain: いい conjugates from よい: よくない, よかった, よくなかった.

meaning: 'Most', 'number one': marks the top of a group, often with 〜の中で or 〜で.

examples.ja: {家族|かぞく}の{中|なか}で{父|ちち}が[[{一番|いちばん}]]{背|せ}が{高|たか}いです。
examples.en: My father is the tallest in my family.

examples.ja: スポーツの{中|なか}でサッカーが[[{一番|いちばん}]]{好|す}きです。
examples.en: Of all sports, I like football the most.

examples.ja: {一年|いちねん}で{八月|はちがつ}が[[{一番|いちばん}]]{暑|あつ}いです。
examples.en: August is the hottest month of the year.

examples.ja: この{店|みせ}で[[{一番|いちばん}]]{安|やす}いのはどれですか。
examples.en: Which is the cheapest one in this shop?

questions.ja: クラスで{木村|きむら}さんが[[{一番|いちばん}]]{若|わか}いです。
questions.en: Kimura is the youngest in the class.
questions.explain: Within a group, the top one is marked with 一番.

questions.ja: {日本|にほん}の{料理|りょうり}で{何|なに}が[[{一番|いちばん}]]{好|す}きですか。
questions.en: What's your favourite Japanese dish?
questions.explain: 一番 + 好き asks which one you like the most.

pattern: Person + と + 一緒に + Verb
meaning: 'Together (with)': doing something along with someone, who is marked with と.

examples.ja: {友達|ともだち}と[[{一緒|いっしょ}に]]{映画|えいが}を{見|み}ました。
examples.en: I watched a film with a friend.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}、[[{一緒|いっしょ}に]]{昼|ひる}ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べませんか。
examples.en: Shall we have lunch together tomorrow?

examples.ja: {毎晩|まいばん}、{家族|かぞく}と[[{一緒|いっしょ}に]]テレビを{見|み}ます。
examples.en: Every evening I watch TV with my family.

examples.ja: {犬|いぬ}と[[{一緒|いっしょ}に]]{公園|こうえん}を{歩|ある}きます。
examples.en: I walk in the park with my dog.

questions.ja: {母|はは}[[と]]{一緒|いっしょ}に{買|か}い{物|もの}に{行|い}きました。
questions.en: I went shopping with my mother.
questions.explain: The person you do something with is marked with と.

questions.ja: {日曜日|にちようび}、{友達|ともだち}と[[{一緒|いっしょ}に]]テニスをしました。
questions.en: On Sunday I played tennis with a friend.
questions.explain: 一緒 needs に to work with a verb: 一緒に.

meaning: 'Always' or 'usually': something that happens every time or as a regular habit.

examples.ja: {朝|あさ}は[[いつも]]パンを{食|た}べます。
examples.en: I always have bread in the morning.

examples.ja: {木村|きむら}さんは[[いつも]]{元気|げんき}ですね。
examples.en: Kimura is always so cheerful.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}は[[いつも]]11{時|じ}に{寝|ね}ます。
examples.en: I always go to bed at eleven.

examples.ja: [[いつも]]{駅|えき}まで{歩|ある}いて{行|い}きます。
examples.en: I always walk to the station.

questions.ja: {父|ちち}は[[いつも]]{朝|あさ}6{時|じ}に{起|お}きます。
questions.en: My father always gets up at six in the morning.
questions.explain: あまり and ぜんぜん need a negative; いつも fits a regular habit.

questions.ja: [[いつも]]{何時|なんじ}に{寝|ね}ますか。
questions.en: What time do you usually go to bed?
questions.explain: いつも in a question asks about your usual habit.

pattern: Noun / な-adj + じゃない / ではない
meaning: 'Is not': the negative of だ / です after a noun or な-adjective. じゃない is spoken and ではない more formal; the polite forms end in ありません.

examples.ja: これは{私|わたし}のかばん[[じゃない]]よ。
examples.en: This isn't my bag.

examples.ja: {父|ちち}は{医者|いしゃ}[[ではありません]]。
examples.en: My father isn't a doctor.

examples.ja: この{辺|へん}はあまり{静|しず}か[[じゃない]]です。
examples.en: This area isn't very quiet.

examples.ja: それは{本当|ほんとう}[[ではない]]。
examples.en: That is not true.

questions.ja: {木村|きむら}さんは{日本人|にほんじん}[[じゃありません]]。
questions.en: Kimura isn't Japanese.
questions.explain: Nouns are negated with じゃありません, never with く.

questions.ja: この{町|まち}は{有名|ゆうめい}[[じゃない]]です。
questions.en: This town isn't famous.
questions.explain: な-adjectives take じゃない; くない is only for い-adjectives.

meaning: At the end of a sentence it makes a question. Between two nouns it means 'or', and after a question word it means 'some-' (誰か, 何か).

examples.ja: これは{何|なん}です[[か]]。
examples.en: What is this?

examples.ja: {明日|あした}、{学校|がっこう}に{来|き}ます[[か]]。
examples.en: Are you coming to school tomorrow?

examples.ja: コーヒー[[か]]{紅茶|こうちゃ}をください。
examples.en: Coffee or tea, please.

examples.ja: {誰|だれ}[[か]]{来|き}ましたよ。
examples.en: Someone's here.

questions.ja: あの{人|ひと}は{誰|だれ}です[[か]]。
questions.en: Who is that person?
questions.explain: か at the end turns the sentence into a question.

questions.ja: {冷蔵庫|れいぞうこ}に{何|なに}[[か]]ありますか。
questions.en: Is there anything in the fridge?
questions.explain: 何か means 'something'; 何も would need a negative.

meaning: 'A or B': lists choices for the listener to pick from. With a verb and its negative it means 'whether or not'.

examples.ja: {肉|にく}か{魚|さかな}[[か]]、どちらがいいですか。
examples.en: Meat or fish, which would you like?

examples.ja: {行|い}く[[か]]{行|い}かないか、まだ{分|わ}かりません。
examples.en: I don't know yet whether I'll go or not.

examples.ja: {土曜日|どようび}[[か]]{日曜日|にちようび}か、どちらが{暇|ひま}ですか。
examples.en: Which day are you free, Saturday or Sunday?

questions.ja: {電車|でんしゃ}[[か]]バスか、どちらで{行|い}きますか。
questions.en: Train or bus, which will you take?
questions.explain: AかBか lists the choices; the first か follows A.

questions.ja: {明日|あした}{来|く}る[[か]]{来|こ}ないか、{電話|でんわ}で{教|おし}えてください。
questions.en: Please call and tell me whether you're coming tomorrow or not.
questions.explain: Verb + か + its negative + か means 'whether or not'.

meaning: After a reason: 'because, so'. After a noun, place or time: 'from', the starting point.

examples.ja: {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}っています[[から]]、{傘|かさ}を{持|も}って{行|い}きます。
examples.en: It's raining, so I'll take an umbrella.

examples.ja: {暑|あつ}い[[から]]、{窓|まど}を{開|あ}けましょう。
examples.en: It's hot, so let's open the window.

examples.ja: {夏休|なつやす}みは{来週|らいしゅう}[[から]]です。
examples.en: The summer holidays start next week.

examples.ja: {家|いえ}[[から]]{駅|えき}まで{歩|ある}いて10{分|ぷん}です。
examples.en: It's a ten-minute walk from my house to the station.

questions.ja: {仕事|しごと}は{朝|あさ}9{時|じ}[[から]]{夕方|ゆうがた}5{時|じ}までです。
questions.en: Work is from 9 in the morning until 5 in the evening.
questions.explain: から marks the starting time; まで marks the end.

questions.ja: {疲|つか}れた[[から]]、{少|すこ}し{休|やす}みましょう。
questions.en: I'm tired, so let's take a short break.
questions.explain: から after a clause gives the reason.

meaning: Verb stem + 方 means 'how to do' or 'the way of doing' it: 読み方, 使い方.

examples.ja: この{漢字|かんじ}の{読|よ}み[[{方|かた}]]を{教|おし}えてください。
examples.en: Please tell me how to read this kanji.

examples.ja: {駅|えき}への{行|い}き[[{方|かた}]]が{分|わ}かりません。
examples.en: I don't know how to get to the station.

examples.ja: {母|はは}にカレーの{作|つく}り[[{方|かた}]]を{習|なら}いました。
examples.en: My mother taught me how to make curry.

examples.ja: このカメラの{使|つか}い[[{方|かた}]]は{難|むずか}しいです。
examples.en: This camera is hard to use.

questions.ja: {日本|にほん}の{手紙|てがみ}の[[{書|か}き{方|かた}]]を{習|なら}いたいです。
questions.en: I want to learn how to write a Japanese letter.
questions.explain: 方 attaches to the ます-stem: 書きます becomes 書き方.

questions.ja: この{果物|くだもの}の[[{食|た}べ{方|かた}]]を{知|し}っていますか。
questions.en: Do you know how to eat this fruit?
questions.explain: For ichidan verbs, drop る and add 方: 食べ方.

meaning: 'But', 'though': joins two contrasting clauses. Casual and very common; it also softens a request or introduces a topic.

examples.ja: この{店|みせ}は{高|たか}い[[けど]]、おいしいです。
examples.en: This place is expensive, but the food is good.

examples.ja: {日本語|にほんご}を{勉強|べんきょう}しています[[けど]]、まだ{下手|へた}です。
examples.en: I'm studying Japanese, but I'm still not good at it.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}{映画|えいが}に{行|い}きます[[けど]]、{一緒|いっしょ}に{行|い}きませんか。
examples.en: I'm going to a film tomorrow. Would you like to come?

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}は{寒|さむ}かった[[けど]]、{今日|きょう}は{暖|あたた}かいね。
examples.en: It was cold yesterday, but today's warm, isn't it?

questions.ja: {部屋|へや}は{狭|せま}い[[けど]]、{駅|えき}から{近|ちか}いです。
questions.en: The room is small, but it's close to the station.
questions.explain: けど attaches straight to the plain form; い-adjectives never take だ.

questions.ja: {今日|きょう}は{日曜日|にちようび}だ[[けど]]、{仕事|しごと}に{行|い}きます。
questions.en: It's Sunday today, but I'm going to work.
questions.explain: After a noun, けど follows だ: 日曜日だけど.

meaning: 'But', 'although': the fuller, more polite form of けど, used in careful speech and writing. けれど sits in between.

examples.ja: {日本|にほん}の{夏|なつ}は{暑|あつ}いです[[けれども]]、{好|す}きです。
examples.en: Japanese summers are hot, but I like them.

examples.ja: {何回|なんかい}も{読|よ}みました[[けれども]]、よく{分|わ}かりませんでした。
examples.en: I read it many times, but I didn't really understand it.

examples.ja: すみません[[けれども]]、{少|すこ}し{待|ま}ってください。
examples.en: I'm sorry, but please wait a moment.

examples.ja: {兄|あに}は{料理|りょうり}が{上手|じょうず}です[[けれど]]、{私|わたし}は{下手|へた}です。
examples.en: My brother is good at cooking, but I'm bad at it.

questions.ja: {薬|くすり}を{飲|の}みました[[けれども]]、まだ{頭|あたま}が{痛|いた}いです。
questions.en: I took some medicine, but I still have a headache.
questions.explain: けれども follows the ます-form directly to show contrast.

questions.ja: {木村|きむら}さんは{学生|がくせい}です[[けれども]]、{毎日|まいにち}{仕事|しごと}をしています。
questions.en: Kimura is a student, but he works every day.
questions.explain: けれども can follow です to join two contrasting clauses.

meaning: With an affirmative verb, 'still'; with a negative, or as まだです, 'not yet'.

examples.ja: {外|そと}は[[まだ]]{明|あか}るいです。
examples.en: It's still light outside.

examples.ja: {子供|こども}たちは[[まだ]]{寝|ね}ています。
examples.en: The children are still asleep.

examples.ja: {兄|あに}は[[まだ]]{学生|がくせい}です。
examples.en: My older brother is still a student.

examples.ja: コーヒーが[[まだ]]{少|すこ}しあります。
examples.en: There's still a little coffee left.

questions.ja: {雨|あめ}が[[まだ]]{降|ふ}っています。
questions.en: It's still raining.
questions.explain: With an affirmative verb, まだ means 'still'.

questions.ja: 「{宿題|しゅくだい}はもう{終|お}わりましたか。」「いいえ、[[まだ]]です。」
questions.en: "Have you finished your homework?" "No, not yet."
questions.explain: いいえ、まだです is the short answer for 'not yet'.

pattern: まだ + Verb-て + いません
meaning: 'Haven't done it yet': for something that hasn't happened so far but still might. The usual answer to もう〜ましたか.

examples.ja: {宿題|しゅくだい}はまだし[[ていません]]。
examples.en: I haven't done my homework yet.

examples.ja: {木村|きむら}さんはまだ{来|き}[[ていません]]。
examples.en: Kimura hasn't arrived yet.

examples.ja: その{映画|えいが}はまだ{見|み}[[ていません]]。
examples.en: I haven't seen that film yet.

examples.ja: {手紙|てがみ}はまだ{書|か}い[[ていません]]。
examples.en: I haven't written the letter yet.

questions.ja: 「もう{昼|ひる}ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べましたか。」「いいえ、まだ{食|た}べ[[ていません]]。」
questions.en: "Have you had lunch yet?" "No, not yet."
questions.explain: 'Not yet' uses まだ + 〜ていません, not the past negative.

questions.ja: {新|あたら}しい{漢字|かんじ}はまだ{覚|おぼ}え[[ていません]]。
questions.en: I haven't learned the new kanji yet.
questions.explain: まだ + 〜ていません: 覚える becomes 覚えていません.
